---
description: "Plain-language meanings of the terms used on Open Island Transit Data."
title: "Plain words"
subtitle: "What the terms on this site mean"
---

::: {.glossary}
Bus location (vehicle position)
: A bus location is where a bus is, as reported by its GPS. Each report also
  says which trip the bus is on, how fast it is going, and how full it is.

Live feed
: The live feed is the stream of bus locations, arrival predictions and
  alerts that Island Transit publishes for trip-planning apps. It uses a
  standard format called GTFS-Realtime. Each update replaces the one before
  it, so nothing is kept unless someone saves it.

Collector
: The collector is this project's program. Every 20 seconds it asks the feed
  for its latest data and saves exactly what comes back.

Schedule (static GTFS)
: The schedule is Island Transit's timetable written in a standard file
  format. It lists every trip, every stop and every scheduled time.

Trip
: A trip is one run of a bus along a route, from its first stop to its last,
  at a scheduled time.

Timepoint
: A timepoint is a stop whose time is printed in Island Transit's timetables.
  Those are the times riders are promised, so that is where we measure
  whether buses are on time.

Departure
: A departure is the moment a bus leaves a timepoint. At the last stop of a
  trip, we use the arrival instead.

On time
: A bus is on time if it leaves no more than 1 minute early and no more than
  5 minutes late. At the last stop, an early arrival also counts as on time.

Typical departure
: The typical departure is the middle value of how early or late the buses
  left, so half left earlier than this and half left later. Statisticians
  call it the median.

Seen (observed)
: A departure is seen when the tracking data was good enough for us to work
  out a time for it. We report the departures we couldn't see separately,
  and we never count them as late.

Service day
: A service day is one calendar day in Pacific time. No Island Transit trip
  runs past midnight, so each trip belongs to exactly one day.

Coverage
: Coverage asks whether every scheduled trip shows up in the tracking at
  all.

Nonresponse
: Nonresponse is data that should be there but is missing, such as a request
  that failed, a feed that came back empty, or a gap in a bus's reports.

Measurement error
: Measurement error is data that is there but wrong. GPS wobble, a bus that
  seems to jump across the map, an old location, and an arrival prediction
  that misses are all examples.

Processing error
: A processing error happens when data can't be matched up, for example when
  the feed names a trip that isn't in the schedule, or a bus can't be tied
  to any trip.

Paradata
: Paradata is data about the data collection itself. It records every
  request the collector made, how long it took, and whether it worked.

Uptime
: Uptime is the share of 20-second time slots in which the collector got a
  good response from the feed.

Arrival prediction
: An arrival prediction is a time like "arriving at 3:42" that the feed gives
  for an upcoming stop. This site checks those predictions against when the
  bus actually arrived.

Release
: A release is a download page on GitHub. Each one holds a month of files.

Parquet
: Parquet is a compact file format for tables. Free tools such as Python, R
  and DuckDB can open it.
:::

The exact definitions behind every number are on the [Methods](methods.qmd)
page.
